card.question: How do you keep a long query readable?

codeExample.text:
WITH paid AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid')
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM paid GROUP BY customer_id

interviewQuestions: When would you use a temp table instead of a CTE?

card.question: How do you keep one row per key when the source sends duplicates?

codeExample.text:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT o.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY loaded_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM orders o
) t
WHERE rn = 1

card.output: One row per order_id: the most recently loaded version.
takeaways: ROW_NUMBER() = 1 per key keeps exactly one row
The ORDER BY decides which duplicate wins
RANK keeps ties, ROW_NUMBER does not
interviewQuestions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK or DENSE_RANK: which one for dedup, and why?
What happens when two rows share the same ORDER BY value?

card.question: How do you insert new rows and update changed ones in one statement?

codeExample.text:
MERGE INTO silver.orders AS t
USING staged AS s ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *

takeaways: The ON condition must match at most one target row
The target keeps state between runs
interviewQuestions: What fails when the source has two rows for one key?
When is a full rebuild simpler than a MERGE?

card.question: How do you find rows with no match?

codeExample.text:
SELECT c.* FROM customers c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)

takeaways: NOT IN breaks on a NULL
interviewQuestions: Why can NOT IN return no rows?
LEFT JOIN … IS NULL or NOT EXISTS?

card.question: How do you avoid shuffling a big table to join a small one?
interviewQuestions: When does a broadcast join fail?

options.title: Partition by the main filter column

decisionCard.question: Partition this table or not?
decisionCard.rule: Partition when most queries filter on one low-cardinality column and each partition still holds large files.
decisionCard.maxim: Design storage around the queries, not around the source.

ask.text: Which column do most queries filter on, and how much data arrives per value?
ask.why: Pruning helps only for the common filter and only with large partitions.

decisionCard.question: Keep only the latest value or the history?
decisionCard.rule: Keep history when someone must report as of a past date or audit a change; otherwise overwrite.
decisionCard.maxim: Define the row before writing the transformation.

ask.text: Does anyone need to know what the value was on a past date?

options.title: Keep the latest row per key

decisionCard.question: How does this pipeline keep one row per key?
decisionCard.rule: Rebuild with ROW_NUMBER() = 1 per key while a full rebuild fits the window; MERGE into a stateful table when volume or late updates make rebuilding too slow.
decisionCard.maxim: Decide what a duplicate is before choosing how to remove it.

ask.text: Can the source send the same key twice, and which version should win?
ask.why: The dedup rule depends on how duplicates arrive and on the business key.

decisionCard.question: Retry automatically or stop the pipeline?
decisionCard.rule: Retry transient failures on idempotent steps; stop on data or code errors that a retry cannot fix.
decisionCard.maxim: Plan for failure before the first production run.

ask.text: Are these steps safe to run twice, and which failures are transient?
ask.why: Only idempotent steps can be retried safely.

decisionCard.question: Full refresh or incremental load?
decisionCard.rule: Refresh fully while the table is small enough to rebuild within the window; go incremental when rebuild time or cost no longer fits.

ask.text: How long does a full rebuild take, and what window do you have?
ask.why: Rebuild time against the window decides the load mode.
